title: The variant that does not come back
hook: A species crashes to 10 animals, then regrows to thousands. Is anything missing?

knows: each animal carries two copies of a gene
doesNotKnow: that a population crash loses rare variants by chance
that regrowing the numbers does not bring a lost variant back

misconception: A population that regrows to its old size is genetically the same as before.
objective: The learner can explain that a crash keeps only the variants that happen to be among the few survivors, so a 1% variant is lost in about 82% of crashes to 10 animals, and regrowth copies the survivors instead of restoring what was lost.

claims.text: If 10 survivors carry 20 gene copies drawn at random, a variant on 1% of copies is missing from all 20 with probability 0.99^20, about 82% (81.6% when the 20 are drawn without replacement from a jar of 1,000 with 10 rare copies, as on the stage).
claims.source: Independent draws: 0.99^20 = 0.8179. Without replacement: product over k = 0..19 of (990 - k)/(1000 - k) = 0.8163. Computed in node (artifacts/scratch/w3life/check.mjs) and in Demo.tsx (P_LOST, P_REPL).

claims.text: On the stage, jar n is drawn with seed n (1, 2, 3 ...); the seeds were not chosen. Over the first 21 jars red is lost in 16; over 100,000 jars drawn the same way it is lost in 81.7%.
claims.source: mulberry32(n) partial Fisher-Yates draw of 20 from 1,000, replicated in artifacts/scratch/w3life/check2.mjs: lost 16 of 21, 82 of 101, 81,658 of 100,000. Seeds untuned (jar number).

claims.text: Regrowth copies the survivors' gene copies, so a variant missing from all survivors cannot return without new mutation or migration; a variant that survives at 1 or 2 of 20 copies comes back at 5% or 10%, a change by chance (drift), not by fitness.
claims.source: Follows from the model (each of 20 copies founds 50 of the 1,000 regrown copies); bottleneck and founder effects, e.g. Hartl & Clark (2007) Principles of Population Genetics, ch. 3.

claims.text: The model is a toy: survivors are random with respect to the gene, and there is no selection, mutation or migration.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; stated in the question ('Toy model'), on the stage ('Toy jar') and in the reveal.

claims.text: Recall: 15 survivors carry 30 copies; a 1% variant is missed by all 30 with probability 0.99^30, about 74%.

recall.question: A bird population falls to 15 birds and later recovers to 10,000. Before the crash, a rare feather variant was carried by 1% of gene copies. What is most likely now?
options: It is back at about 1%, because the numbers recovered
It is probably gone, and regrowth alone cannot bring it back
It is more common, because survivors are the fittest
recall.why: Thirty copies drawn at random probably miss a 1% variant (0.99^30 is about 74%), and regrowth only copies what survived.
